about.title: Bell Gardens Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Bell Gardens is a dense, walkable city along Florence and Gage Avenues, where residents move between shops, apartments, and bus stops on foot every day. That kind of foot traffic means uneven pavement, wet floors, cluttered stairwells, and poorly lit parking lots can turn into real hazards fast. If you were hurt on someone else's property here, California law requires proof that the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to correct it or warn you. That's why documentation matters so much — photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can make or break a claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free referral service that connects injured Bell Gardens residents with independent attorneys who handle these cases on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover compensation for you. Reaching out early helps preserve evidence before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Bell Gardens Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Fast Action Protects Surveillance Footage
items.desc: Stores and apartment complexes in Bell Gardens often overwrite security video within days or weeks. Connecting with an attorney quickly can mean the difference between having that footage preserved or losing it forever.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery reduced by your share of fault, rather than blocking your claim outright.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Bell Gardens?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If your fall happened on government-owned property, such as a public sidewalk or city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. Because these timelines are strict, it helps to talk with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell in a store on Florence or Gage Avenue and no employee saw it happen?
items.answer: You don't need an eyewitness employee for a valid claim, but you do need evidence that the hazard existed and that the owner had a reasonable chance to notice and fix it. Photos of the spill or defect, receipts showing when you were there, and any store surveillance video can all help establish this. An attorney can request that footage before it's deleted.

items.question: Will my claim be denied if I was partly distracted when I fell?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows a pure comparative fault system, meaning your compensation could be reduced by your percentage of responsibility, but you can still recover for the portion attributable to the property owner. This is something an independent attorney can evaluate based on the specific facts of your fall.
